* WHAT...Water levels of 2 to 4 feet above the normal high tide
expected during the Thursday and Friday high tides.

* WHERE...Hooper Bay.

* IMPACTS...Beach property, the lowest buildings, and the access

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 527 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located near Siren, or 22 miles east of Pine City, moving
northeast at 50 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree damage is
likely.

This dangerous storm will be near...
Siren and Webster around 530 PM CDT.
Saint Croix Band Pike Lake Area around 535 PM CDT.
Saint Croix Band Sand Lake Area around 540 PM CDT.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 527 PM CDT, broadcast media reported strong thunderstorms along a
line extending from near Rose Creek to 6 miles southeast of Rockwell.
Movement was northeast at 50 mph.

HAZARD...Penny to dime size hail.

SOURCE...Broadcast media.

IMPACT...Minor hail damage to vegetation is possible.

Strong thunderstorms will be near...
Osage, Rockford, Adams, Stacyville, Rose Creek, Rudd, and Marble
Rock around 535 PM CDT.
Grand Meadow and Floyd around 545 PM CDT.
Charles City around 550 PM CDT.

Other locations impacted by these storms include Meyer, Toeterville,
County Roads B 60 And T 18, Rock Creek, Idlewilde State Park,
Roseville, Brownville, County Roads T 54 And A 31, Oakwood, and
County Roads 4 And 8.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 6 and
12 inches near Red Dog Mine and 12 to 18 inches in the Western
Brooks Range. Winds gusting as high as 35 mph.

* WHERE...Red Dog Mine and the South Slopes of the Western Brooks
Range.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Areas of blowing snow
could significantly reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Mostly rain is expected below 800 feet. The
heaviest precipitation is expected Tuesday and Wednesday. The
heaviest snow is expected Wednesday. Temperatures cool Wednesday
into Thursday.

events.region: Northern Denali Borough; Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...South winds 30 to 45 mph with gusts up to 65 mph expected.

* WHERE...Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp and Windy Pass.

* WHEN...Until 7 AM AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A brief lull in winds is expected Thursday
morning before southerly winds quickly strengthen again Thursday
afternoon. During this time, sustained winds in the Eastern Alaska
Range will range from 45 to 55 mph, gusting up to 80 mph. In the
Western Alaska Range, sustained winds will range from 35 to 45 mph,
gusting up to 70 mph.

events.region: Silver Bay Harbor to Two Harbors MN; Two Harbors to Duluth MN; Duluth MN to Port Wing WI; Port Wing to Sand Island WI; Lake Superior west of a line from Saxon Harbor WI to Grand Portage MN beyond 5NM
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
SMWDLH

The National Weather Service in Duluth MN has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Duluth MN to Port Wing WI...
Lake Superior west of a line from Saxon Harbor WI to Grand Portage
MN beyond 5NM...
Port Wing to Sand Island WI...
Silver Bay Harbor to Two Harbors MN...
Two Harbors to Duluth MN...

* Until 615 PM CDT.

* At 520 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 8 nm southwest of Superior Harbor, or 12 nm
south of Duluth Lift Bridge Channel, moving northeast at 40 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts, wind gusts to 40 knots, and large hail.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves. Large hail could
result in structural damage.

* Locations impacted include...
Superior Entry, Knife River Marina, Castle Danger, Barkers Island,
Duluth Harbor, Duluth Lift Bridge Channel, Twin Points Safe Harbor,
Two Harbors Protected Access Agate Bay, Brule Point, McQuade
Harbor, Superior Harbor, Larsmont, Stoney Point, French River, and
Port Wing Harbor.

events.summary:
At 413 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the
warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of South Central Otero County.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...High astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low
lying areas around Humboldt Bay. Up to one half foot of
saltwater inundation above ground level is possible near
shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 9.0 and 9.3 feet MLLW
at the North Spit tide gauge is predicted.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...From 1 PM to 4 PM PDT Thursday. High tide is at 1:59 PM
at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation
will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay
including parks and roads with only isolated closures expected.
Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in the Arcata
Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Visibility one quarter mile or less at
times. Total snow accumulations 7 to 15 inches.

* WHERE...Northern Susitna Valley, including the Parks Highway
corridor through Broad Pass.

* WHEN...From 1 PM Thursday to 2 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult, with low visibility and
rapidly accumulating snow along the Parks Highway.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Light snow will fall overnight tonight through
Thursday morning, with 3 to 6 inches accumulation. Snowfall
intensity will then increase during the afternoon hours. The
heaviest snow will fall Thursday night through Friday morning. Snow
could then mix with or change to rain Friday afternoon as
temperatures warm above freezing.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Southern Susitna Valley; Central Susitna Valley
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Snow, freezing rain, and rain expected. Total snow
accumulations up to two inches and ice accumulation up to one tenth
of an inch.

* WHERE...The Susitna Valley, from around Willow north to the
Talkeetna Spur Road.

* WHEN...From 2 AM to 1 PM AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
will impact the Thursday morning commute. Roads, and especially
bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Light snow will develop around midnight
tonight. Warmer air aloft will then cause a mix of precipitation
types late tonight through Thursday morning with a general
transition from snow to freezing rain. The willow area, which tends
to hold on to colder surface temperatures has the highest potential
for freezing rain. Surface temperatures will slowly rise above
freezing late Thursday morning through Thursday afternoon, with a
changeover to plain rain.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Visibility one half mile or less at times.
Total snow accumulations 10 to 15 inches.

* WHERE...Thompson Pass.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Friday to 4 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Light snow will develop Thursday evening, then
intensify Thursday night into Friday. The heaviest snow is expected
during the day Friday. Warming temperatures on Friday will lead to
a changeover to rain for lower elevations of the pass. The top of
the pass will likely remain all snow.
